extracted.intended_audience: senior/key personnel and other significant contributors preparing NIH-format biographical sketches and research support sections for NIH grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing NIH-format biographical sketches (biosketches) and Research Support entries for senior/key personnel and other significant contributors, following the NIH/OMB (Rev.03/2020) format and page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified NIH biosketch format and headings (A. Personal Statement, B. Positions and Honors, C. Contributions to Science, D. Research Support). Keep each individual's biosketch to a maximum of five pages; maintain section ordering and headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Include NAME; eRA COMMONS USER NAME (credential, e.g., agency login); POSITION TITLE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide exact name as on application, include eRA Commons user name, and current position title. These fields appear at the top of the biosketch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education/Training (table)
rubrics_metrics.description: EDUCATION/TRAINING (Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, include postdoctoral training and residency training if applicable. Add/delete rows as necessary.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List institution and location, degree (if applicable), completion date (MM/YYYY), and field of study. Start with undergraduate (baccalaureate) and include subsequent training (graduate, postdoc, residency). Use a table or rows; add or delete rows as needed to cover training history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise narrative describing the individual's research focus, relevant experience, qualifications for the role on the project, mentoring experience if relevant, and why they are well suited to contribute to the proposed work. Use examples that highlight key contributions, collaborations, and mentoring roles (as illustrated in the sample personal statements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Positions and Honors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List professional positions (with dates) in chronological order and include honors/awards. Present positions with dates and brief role titles; list honors separately. The sample shows year ranges and institution/role formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributions to Science
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numbered descriptions of up to several major contributions or research themes. For each contribution include a short narrative explaining the significance and context, followed by key representative publications (citations, PMIDs/PMCIDs when available). Use the sample style: numbered items, narrative paragraph, then lettered citations (a., b., c.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Support (ongoing and completed)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate ongoing and completed research support. For each entry include grant number, PI name, funding agency (NIH institute), project title, project dates, and the individual's role (e.g., PI, Co-I, Project Leader, Core Leader, Subproject Co-PI). Provide a brief description of project goals/specific aims or overarching hypothesis as shown in the sample entries. Include exact dates and note whether the support is active or completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide complete publication list link
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete List of Published Work in My Bibliography: [URL]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a link (e.g., My Bibliography or Google Scholar) to the applicant's complete list of published work to complement the representative publications listed under 'Contributions to Science'.
